questions.text: A tension member (tie rod) in a pin-jointed truss has an effective length KL = 4.5 m and radius of gyration r = 18 mm. Calculate KL/r and determine if it meets the preferred slenderness standard for tension.

options.text: KL/r = 200; non-compliant (exceeds preferred 300)
KL/r = 250; compliant (below preferred 300)
KL/r = 300; on the boundary; marginally acceptable
KL/r = 250; non-compliant for tension (compression limit applies)

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: KL/r = 4500 mm ÷ 18 mm = 250. This is less than 300 and meets the maximum slenderness limit for tension members.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: In a bolted connection between two C-channels (back-to-back), the engineer must provide a transition element to distribute concentrated load. What is this component called?

options.text: Shear connector
Gusset plate
Shear stud
Splice plate

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: A gusset plate is a transition piece (often triangular or rectangular) that distributes concentrated load from a member into fasteners or welds. It handles stress concentration.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.code_citation: AISC Steel Construction Manual, Part 9: Connections

questions.text: A compression member in a braced frame has KL/r = 185. Is this member compliant with slenderness limits, and what is the governing standard value?

options.text: Non-compliant; KL/r must be ≤ 150, according to standard design codes for structural stability
Compliant; maximum allowed is 200 for compression
Compliant; maximum allowed is 300, which applies to specific cases under certain conditions
Non-compliant; AISC has no upper limit for compression, but practical limits are often applied

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: AISC 360-16 Section E3 sets maximum KL/r = 200 for compression members. KL/r = 185 is well below this threshold and is compliant.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: Which of the following section types is most appropriate for a bracing member that must resist a tensile pull in a truss?

options.text: W-section (wide flange)
S-section (American standard)
L-section (angle)
T-section (tee)

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.b: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: L-angles are standard for truss bracing because they are lightweight, handle pure tension well, and connect easily via bolts through a single leg.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: A wide-flange section (W610×82) is used as a primary beam in a building frame. The web develops local buckling near the point of concentrated load. To prevent this failure, which component should be welded to the section?

options.text: Gusset plate
Web stiffener
Shear connector
Splice plate

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: A web stiffener (vertical steel plate) is welded transversely across the web to prevent local buckling and bearing failure under concentrated loads. This is standard practice near reactions and heavy loads.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.code_citation: AISC Steel Construction Manual, Part 9: Design for Concentrated Forces

questions.text: A W460×89 section is selected for a primary column in a braced frame. What does the '460' refer to?

options.text: Flange width in millimeters, which is critical for determining the load distribution across the section.
Depth of the section in millimeters
Moment of inertia in 10⁶ mm⁴, a measure of the section's resistance to bending.
Section modulus in 10³ mm³, indicating the strength of the section in resisting bending moments.

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: W-sections are designated W(depth)×(unit weight). W460×89 means 460 mm deep (nominal), 89 kg/m unit weight.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.code_citation: AISC Steel Construction Manual, 15th ed., Part 1: Dimensions and Properties

questions.text: A truss node is formed by welding three members: two diagonals and one vertical. The engineer elects to minimize stress concentration by designing a large triangular gusset plate. However, field inspection reveals the gusset plate is not fully welded to the vertical member along its entire edge. What is the consequence?

options.text: The vertical member will experience bending instead of pure axial compression, which can lead to unexpected structural behavior
Stress concentration will concentrate at the toe of the partial weld, potentially causing fatigue crack initiation
The gusset plate will slip and allow excessive joint rotation, which is a common misconception about weld integrity
The joint will experience no adverse effect; partial welds are acceptable in modern design, which is incorrect as full welds are typically required for structural integrity

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: Partial welds create a discontinuity and a stress concentration at the weld termination (toe). Under cyclic loading (common in highway bridges and industrial frames), this is a fatigue crack initiation point. Full penetration and continuous welds are required.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.code_citation: AISC 360-16, Section J2: Welds. AWS D1.1: Structural Welding Code—Steel

questions.text: An engineer selects a C-section (channel) for a purlin in a roof structure and orients the channel with its web horizontal (opening downward). Later, it is discovered that this orientation reduces the bending strength by ~25% compared to a vertical web orientation. Explain the structural reason.

options.text: Horizontal webs have lower shear capacity, which can lead to increased deflection and potential structural failure under load
The neutral axis shifts when the web is horizontal, reducing moment arm, which affects the overall structural integrity and load distribution
The section modulus decreases because the flanges are no longer the furthest fibers from the neutral axis; bending strength depends on flange distance and web contribution
Horizontal channels are never acceptable for purlins due to their inability to effectively distribute loads across the span

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.b: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: Section modulus S = I/c, where c is the distance from neutral axis to extreme fiber. With a vertical web (typical), the flanges are the furthest fibers. With a horizontal web, the geometry inverts; the effective moment arm and section modulus decline, reducing bending capacity.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.code_citation: AISC Steel Construction Manual, Part 1: Section Properties and Orientation

questions.text: A long tied-arch bridge has main tie rods made from L-sections (angles). The effective length is KL = 12 m and the selected angle has r_min = 25 mm (minimum radius of gyration). Calculate KL/r and evaluate whether this design is at risk if the tie rod transitions from dead load (tension) to wind-induced oscillation (potential compression due to aeroelastic flutter). Assume AISC limits: tension ≤ 300, compression ≤ 200.

options.text: KL/r = 480; non-compliant for both tension and compression; angle is undersized and may require redesign
KL/r = 480; non-compliant for both tension (exceeds 300) and compression (exceeds 200); angle is undersized with risk if flutter induces compression
KL/r = 300; marginally acceptable for tension and compression; no risk, but close monitoring is advised
KL/r = 480; acceptable for all loads under AISC flexibility provisions for special bridges, though this is rarely applicable

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: KL/r = 12,000 mm ÷ 25 mm = 480.This exceeds both limits (300 preferred for tension, 200 for compression). The tie rod is non-compliant even as a primary tension member.ons, but if wind flutter induces local compression reversals, the 480 ratio far exceeds the 200 compression limit. The design is at risk.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.code_citation: AISC 360-16, Section E3: Slenderness Limits. ASCE Guideline 6-19: Aeroelastic Effects on Structures

questions.text: A hollow structural section (HSS) is selected over a built-up section for a heavily loaded column. What is the primary advantage of HSS?

options.text: Lower fabrication cost, which can be significant in large-scale projects
Higher section modulus per unit weight, providing better structural efficiency
Closed section geometry and uniform torsional rigidity
Easier field splicing without welding, reducing on-site labor requirements

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.b: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: HSS is a closed section, providing symmetrical properties, high torsional stiffness, and uniform strength in all directions. Built-up sections are open and require bracing for torsion.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.code_citation: AISC Steel Construction Manual, Part 1: Section Properties
